Monsignor Capel, it is announced by the
official journal of the Vatican, has been named
Domestic Prelate of his Holiness. This ap-
pointment entitles the distinguished nominee
to the honours of a bishop.

From _Paris it is announced that the Duke
of Edinburgh has there commenced a Conti,
ner.tal tour. Ile travels incognito, under the
title of the Earl of Kent.

M. Thiers has virtually won his hard and
prolonged battle for the duties on raw material.
The general debate was closed on Saturday,
and forty-eight clauses of the first section of
the new tariff were adopted.

On Saturday last Mr. Robert Stroud, an
old servant of the Post-office, went with his
sou from Bampion, in Oxfordshire, to the
Thames, for the purpose of bathing and
fishing. The son on entering the water got
out of his depth, and Mr. Stroud at once
plunged in to save him, but he not only
failed to do so, but also lost his own life, both
being drowned.

On Tuesday the two Mines Regulation Bills
passed their second reading in the House of
Lords ; and the Elementary Eduoation
(Elections) Bill, the second reading of which
was moved by Lord Ripon was thrown out
on the instance of Lord Salisbury, hy 46 to
42. .

in the House of Commons, on Tuesday, Mr.
Gladstone, replying to Sir Robert Peel, amid
a scene of some confusion, indicated that it
was not tho intention of the Government to
enforce against Jesuits expelled from Germany
any provisions of the Act of 1829 which might
prevent their entrance into this country.

It is stated that Mr. Gladstone has arranged
to pay his visit to Ireland. early in October.
Ho will be accompanied by Mr. John Bright
Ind Lord Spencer, and will address meetings
in Dublin, Belfast, Londonderry, and probably
in Cork. 11r. Bright, if he feels equal to the
task, will speak at one or two of these places.

During the week ending Saturday last
5,252 births and 3,278 deaths were registered
in London and twenty other large cities and
towns of the United Kingdom. The mortality
from all causes in these towns was at the rate
of 23 deaths annually to every 1,000 persons
estimated to be living. In London 2,151
births and 1,407 deaths were registered last
week. The births were 22 and the deaths
144 below the average numbers in the corre-
sponding week of the last ten years. The
annual death rate rose from 20 per 1,000 in
the previous week to 23 last week.

Her Majesty's Ministers were entertained at
the Mansion House on Wednesday night. A.
brilliant company assembled, and most of the
Members of the Cabinet were present. Mr.
Gosehen responded for the navy, Mr. Glad-
stone for the Ministry, the Lord Chancellor
for the House of Lords, and Mr. Bruce for the
Commons; the Marquis of Ripon proposing
$' The Ladies."

A great seizure of Imperialist pamphlets has
'been made in what was once the 'Aloe of the
Potpie Francais, and a voluminous eorre-
spoadeneelias also been discovered.

The trial of Marshal Bazaine is expected
to commence about the Ist of October. It is
stated that two hundred witnesses will be
called, and that already three thousand docti-
meats have been deposited with Marshal
Baragusy d'Hilliers.

Another tremendous thunderstorm bnrst
over London on Tuesday evening, between
six and seven o'clock, the flashes of lightning;
being almost unintermittent, and the peals of
thunder singularly impressive. A consider-
able amount of damage was done in various
parts of the metropolis by the lightning
and rain' the roads in some places being
flooded. At Brixton a church was struck by
the electric fluid; awl in 131ackwall some mills
were set on fire. Several people were struck
down in the street, some of them being severely
injured,.

Thomas Moore tried before Mr. Baron
Bramwell, on the charge of having strangled
his wife in a field near Ashford, in Loot, was
found guilty and sentenced to death.

A temperance festival at the Crystal Palace,
under the auspices of the National Temperance
-
League, was very numerously attended,, and
on the whole successful. The" noveLe xperi-
went" of-forbidding the sale of all ititexicatin4
drinks at-the refresment bars was tried ; but
not a MAU propoitioa of the crowd, either
belonging to the general public, or recognizing
'a distinction between temperance and tuba.
Atiropee, evinced decided 'displeasure at the.
innovation.

The King of Spain has arrived at Santander,
and has been received by the population wall
joyous acclamations.

Charles 'Sylvester Bore, styling himself, a
clergyman, again appeared before Mr. Newton
on the charge of obtaining money under false
pretences. 'At the conclusion of the evidence,.
the magistrate, strongly animadverting on the
conduct of the defendant, said that there was
not sufficient legal evidence to send the ease
to a jury, and diseharged Mr. Bore, who, in
leaving the doc 4, objected to the expressions
which Mr. Newton had used,

The troops at Aldershot were reviewed by the
Duke of Cambridge, and a sham fight after-
wards look place in Long Valley, on Wednes-
day. General Sir Hope Grant commanded
the cavalry, his Royal Highness directing the
general movements. Against an enemy sup-
posed to be secreted somewhere in the direc-
tion of Cove Common, a series of manceuvres
were instituted, and a very hot action was
the result, a brilliant cavalry charge being
led by Sir Hope Grant in person. In the end
a general advance was made, and, the enemy
being defeated at all points, the tiring ceased
about one o'clock. After a march past the
troops returned into camp, and the Duke of
Cambridge to London. •

After a brief delay the power of the Judicial
Committee of the Privy Council to deal with
Mr. Purchas has been defined. Their lordships
have decided that no precedent exists of sum-
marily depriving a clerk of his benefice for
disobedience of an order of suspension; but
they consider that all the posVers of the COurt
of Delegates have been transferred to them,
and they therefore direct that an order be
issued suspending Mr. Purehas ab Oki° et
beiti:fleio for one year from the present time.

At Clerkenwell Police-court a statement
was made exonerating Price Humphreys, the
man lately suspected of being concerned in the
Hoxton murders. It appears that the blood
on the bag was caused by the priboner's carry-
ing some lambs' heads therein. Humphreys,
who was committed for trial. on the charge of
passing counterfeit coin, was incidentally
stated to have been at one time in 'a good
position of life, having carried on business in
the city s, a wine merchant and married the
niece of an M.P. -

In the French Assembly the tax on silks
has been voted by 319 against 232. The
whole of the first article, relating to raw
material, was also passed by 317 against 233
fotes. It is now thought that the Assembly
will separate on the 4th of August, although
the policy of doing so is much questioned.

In reference to the late attack on the
King of Spain, it is 3 stated, on the part of the
Spanish Government, that he was duly warned
that an attempt would be made upon his life,
and that his Majesty disregarded the hint.
The Government adreit's that it was unable to
indicate the precise nature of the anticipated
attack. '

*At Camden Park, Chislehurst, the Emperor
Napoleon, replying to an address presented
by a Sunday-school to whom he had lent the
use of the grounds, expressed himself as
greatly interested in the education of the
young. His Majesty also adverted with
pleasure to the manner in wlliph he had been
everywhere received in England.

We read of a most determined and resolute
thief in Middlefield, Conn. He removed the
corner-stone of a church and stole a few coins
which had been Aeposited there for the eyes
of far distant generations, thus accomplishing
the entirely novel feat of stealing from pos-
terity. An indignant religious newspaper
compares this to "the theft of acorns from a
blind hog," which strikes us as a fresh and
satisfactory simile.— -Yew York Tribune.

A railway accident occurred on Wednesday
morning at the Black-lane station of the Lan-
cashire and Yorkshire Railway, between Bury
and Bolton. A coal train started from
Bradley Fold station for Blue Pits at eight in
the morning, and had not gone far when the
axle of a waggon broke, capsizing the waggons
and contents. At this moment a train from
Manchester to Liverpool ran into the broken-
down train. No lives were lost,

' At the Mansion House police court on Mon-
day William Lake, a 'City clerk and cashier,
was charged with embezzling from his employ
era, Messrs. Newsom, Burke, and Co., at

£l,BOO in all. Of this he had given back

committed the prisoner for trial.
